I have been led into a deserted and inaccessible place. It happened for destruction and loss. For the shepherds were foolish and did not seek the Lord, therefore the whole flock did not understand and was scattered. The shepherds were truly foolish and became a cause of destruction for the people under their hand. Although they should have been a way for others to believe in Christ, they sought glory from men and did not seek the glory that comes from God alone. If they believed in Moses, they would have believed in him, for Moses wrote about him. They became blind and leaders of the blind. They were destroyed and fell into the pits of destruction. What then does the prophet try to do by advising them to choose better thoughts and to try the words of the Savior? He mixes the rebuke with the advice, healing the wounds of their evil counsel with a varied remedy. Thus, he says, hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom, and attend to the law of God, people of Gomorrah. You hear how he brings a rod of love and divine thought to the people and rulers, striking those who are greatly diseased with disobedience. He compares the most impious cities to Jerusalem, which had the most immeasurable sin and did not have any complete righteousness within itself…

For God was planning to destroy the cities of the Sodomites and informed Abraham about it, and Abraham responded to Him. God promised that if ten righteous people were found in Sodom, He would spare the city from His wrath. However, no righteous people were found. Therefore, the cities received punishments equal to their wicked deeds. Such was the condition of Jerusalem, which had a small number of righteous people. The prophet Jeremiah lamented about Jerusalem. God said to search the streets of Jerusalem for anyone who does justice and seeks faith, and if found, He would be merciful. Since Jerusalem was corrupt and polluted, God called it Sodom and Gomorrah, and its leaders and people were guilty of the same uncleanness as Sodom.
pass_b_english: …It became for me an unapproachable wilderness. It resulted in destruction and loss. For the shepherds were truly foolish and did not seek the Lord; because of this, the whole flock did not understand and was scattered. The shepherds were indeed foolish, and they became a cause of destruction for the people under their hand.

Moreover, how was it that they should not have been a way for others to believe in Christ, having been greatly instructed through law and prophets, to be a path for others to believe in him? Or does the Savior say that he received glory from man and did not seek the glory that comes from God alone? For if they believed in Moses, they would have believed in him, for he wrote about him. They have indeed become blind and leaders of the blind. In this way they have also slipped and have fallen into the pits of destruction.

What then does the prophet attempt to do by advising them with good exhortations: to cause the declining to think well, and to test the words of the Savior? He mixes, however, the rebuke with the exhortations in a medicinal way, with a varied remedy, healing the wounds of their evil counsel. Thus, he says, 'Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; attend to the law of God, people of Gomorrah.' You hear how he brings a rod of love and divine thought to the people and rulers, and strikes many who are diseased with disobedience.

To the most impious cities, he exhorts Jerusalem, as being the greatest in immeasurable sin and not having anyone completely righteous within itself… For God was planning to destroy the cities of the Sodomites and made the matter known to Abraham; and he [responded] to Him, 'Will you destroy the righteous with the wicked? And shall the righteous be as the wicked?' (Genesis 18:24-25). God promised that if ten righteous people were found in Sodom, He would spare the cities from His wrath. But He did not find them. For they had received punishments equal to their own impieties. Such was the condition of Jerusalem, having a small portion of the righteous.

And indeed the prophet Jeremiah lamented for her. And God said, 'Run through the streets of Jerusalem, and see, and seek, and look in her squares, if you find a man who does justice and seeks faith, so that I may be merciful to her' (Jeremiah 5:1).
